banner.title: HIGH-LEVEL CHARACTERS OPENS - DMO Chapter 7, round one of five: the saving-throw improvement limits by group (priest 19, rogue 21, warrior 17, wizard 21, read from the PHB Table 60 reference), the automatic saving-throw failure doctrine (the universal fail on 3 or less on 1d20, the lesser-deity 2, the intermediate 1, the greater never, the bonus-proof and always-a-chance rules, the adjusted-roll reading of 3-or-less numbers, the Wulf worked example reading 5 - 3 = 2 with the actual 1, 2 or 3 still failing), the Table 36 saving-throw grid (28 rows in four group bands by the defender-minus-caster difference: priest 7 rows, rogue 6, warrior 10, wizard 5, in the paralyzation-or-death, petrification-or-polymorph and spell columns) with its four row-band chains, the Table 37 device casting levels (rod 12, staff 8, wand 6, other item 12, artifact 20), the Table 38 caster-level penalty ladder (0 at 1-12 down to -6 at 28-30, the either-or rule that excludes Table 36 in favor of the PHB Table 60), and the Table 39 THACO limits (priest 8, rogue 11, warrior 1, wizard 14, the attack roll of 1 always a miss, monsters unlimited).
banner.provenance: verified against printed pp. 142-144 of the archive.org DMO captures (items dungeon-master-option-high-level-campaigns and tsr02156dmsoptionhighlevelcampaigns, the djvu.txt full texts, leaf N = printed page N; the tsr02156 ABBYY read is primary and the tesseract read is cross-checked - its two misreads noted here: the fails-on-5-or-less for the printed 3-or-less, and the -1-to-5 row for the printed -1 to -3); the save limits and the auto-failure doctrine from p. 142, the Table 36 grid, the footnote worked examples and the usage doctrine from p. 143, the Tables 37 through 39 from p. 144. The Wulf example is pinned verbatim: the -3 poison penalty succeeds on 5 or higher while an actual 1, 2 or 3 still fails.
banner.sentinel: the gap census after this round: 84 closed, 12 open - five Chapter 7 children flip in round one of five (the parent stays open until R612); the DMO arc continues with R609 (Tables 40-41 plus the Warriors with Table 42).

consts.name: dewPriestSaveLimitLevel
consts.comment: the improvement cap: priests reach a level beyond which saving throws cannot be further improved, at level 19 (printed p. 142).

consts.name: dewRogueSaveLimitLevel
consts.comment: the improvement cap: rogues reach the saving-throw limit at level 21 (printed p. 142).

consts.name: dewWarriorSaveLimitLevel
consts.comment: the improvement cap: warriors reach the saving-throw limit at level 17 (printed p. 142).

consts.name: dewWizardSaveLimitLevel
consts.comment: the improvement cap: wizards reach the saving-throw limit at level 21 (printed p. 142).

consts.name: dewPhbSaveTable
consts.comment: the reference table: the group save limits are read from Table 60 in the Player's Handbook (printed p. 142; referenced, not reprinted).

consts.name: dewAutoFailMortal
consts.comment: the universal failure floor: all characters and most other creatures fail their saving throws on rolls of 3 or less on 1d20 (printed p. 142).

consts.name: dewAutoFailLesserDeity
consts.comment: the lesser-deity failure floor: lesser deities fail their saving throws on rolls of 2 or less (printed p. 142).

consts.name: dewAutoFailIntermediateDeity
consts.comment: the intermediate-deity failure floor: intermediate deities fail on rolls of 1 (printed p. 142).

consts.name: dewAutoFailGreaterDeity
consts.comment: the greater-deity failure floor: greater deities need not roll at all - they never fail; the fail number is zero (printed p. 142).

consts.name: dewT36RowCount
consts.comment: the Table 36 row count: 28 rows in four group bands - priest 7, rogue 6, warrior 10, wizard 5 (printed p. 143).

consts.name: dewRogueRowBase
consts.comment: the rogue row base: the rogue bands of Table 36 sit at grid rows 7 through 12 (printed p. 143).

consts.name: dewWarriorRowBase
consts.comment: the warrior row base: the warrior bands of Table 36 sit at grid rows 13 through 22 (printed p. 143).

consts.name: dewWizardRowBase
consts.comment: the wizard row base: the wizard bands of Table 36 sit at grid rows 23 through 27 (printed p. 143).

consts.name: dewT38BandCount
consts.comment: the Table 38 band count: seven caster-level bands, 1-12 through 28-30 plus the beyond-30 tail (printed p. 144).

consts.name: dewWulfParSaveNumber
consts.comment: the Wulf worked example: Wulf, a 21st-level priest, has a saving-throw number of 2 against paralyzation, poison or death magic (printed p. 143).

consts.name: dewWulfPoisonPenalty
consts.comment: the Wulf worked example: a particularly virulent poison imposes a -3 penalty to the saving throw (printed p. 143).

consts.name: dewWulfSuccessRoll
consts.comment: the Wulf worked example: the save succeeds on a roll of 5 or higher - the roll beats the automatic-failure number and still equals 2 after the -3 modifier (printed p. 143).

consts.name: dewRodLevel
consts.comment: the device casting level: a rod attacks at caster level 12 (Table 37, printed p. 144).

consts.name: dewStaffLevel
consts.comment: the device casting level: a staff attacks at caster level 8 (Table 37, printed p. 144).

consts.name: dewWandLevel
consts.comment: the device casting level: a wand attacks at caster level 6 (Table 37, printed p. 144).

consts.name: dewOtherItemLevel
consts.comment: the device casting level: any other magical item attacks at caster level 12 (Table 37, printed p. 144).

consts.name: dewArtifactLevel
consts.comment: the device casting level: an artifact attacks at caster level 20 (Table 37, printed p. 144).

consts.name: dewThacoLimitPriest
consts.comment: the THACO limit: a priest's THACO advancement stops at 8 (Table 39, printed p. 144).

consts.name: dewThacoLimitRogue
consts.comment: the THACO limit: a rogue's THACO advancement stops at 11 (Table 39, printed p. 144).

consts.name: dewThacoLimitWarrior
consts.comment: the THACO limit: a warrior's THACO advancement stops at 1 - warriors improve THACO the most (Table 39, printed p. 144).

consts.name: dewThacoLimitWizard
consts.comment: the THACO limit: a wizard's THACO advancement stops at 14 (Table 39, printed p. 144).

consts.name: dewAutoMissRoll
consts.comment: the automatic miss: no matter what the attacker's THACO, an attack roll of 1 is always a miss (printed p. 144).

bools.name: dewAutoFailAlwaysPossible
bools.comment: the always-a-chance rule: barring a special circumstance that makes the save unnecessary (a successful magic-resistance roll, immunity to the attack form), there is always a chance a character can fail (printed p. 142).

bools.name: dewAutoFailIgnoresBonuses
bools.comment: the bonus-proof rule: the automatic failure stands no matter how many bonuses the roll receives from magical items, spells, ability scores and the like (printed p. 142).

bools.name: dewSaveNumberIsAdjustedRoll
bools.comment: the adjusted-roll reading: a saving-throw success number of 3 or less from Table 60 or Table 36 refers to the character's adjusted die roll, not the actual number rolled (printed p. 143).

bools.name: dewGreaterDeityNeverFails
bools.comment: the greater-deity immunity: greater deities need not roll at all - they never fail their saving throws (printed p. 142).

bools.name: dewT36ForDuelsOnly
bools.comment: the intended use: Table 36 is intended primarily for magical dueling, see Chapter 5; in regular play it is somewhat cumbersome (printed p. 143).

bools.name: dewT36NotForNonSpells
bools.comment: the non-spell exclusion: saving throws against poisons, breath weapons, or any other attack that is not a spell or spell-like ability from a creature or device use the standard saving-throw tables, not Table 36 (printed p. 143).

bools.name: dewDeviceClosestColumn
bools.comment: the device column rule: rods, staves, wands and other magical devices use the Table 36 column that is closest to their effects (printed p. 143).

bools.name: dewWielderLevelIrrelevant
bools.comment: the device-level rule: the wielder's level or Hit Dice is irrelevant when a device is used - the device type determines the attacker's level (printed p. 143).

bools.name: dewDmConcealsCasterLevel
bools.comment: the concealment doctrine: during play the DM should conceal the attacker's true level of power - announce the attack form, then the success or failure on the adjusted roll (printed p. 143).

bools.name: dewT38ExcludesT36
bools.comment: the either-or rule: if you use Table 38, do not use Table 36; use Table 60 from the Player's Handbook instead (printed p. 144).

bools.name: dewFireballUsesSpellColumn
bools.comment: the worked device example: a fireball from a wand of fire uses the spell column of Table 36 (printed p. 143).

bools.name: dewWandParalyzationUsesParColumn
bools.comment: the worked device example: a paralyzation beam from a wand of paralyzation uses the paralyzation or death magic column (printed p. 143).

bools.name: dewThacoAdvancementLimited
bools.comment: the limit doctrine: a character's THACO advancement is limited - professional skills and training extend a creature's natural talents only so far (printed p. 144).

bools.name: dewWarriorsImproveThacoMost
bools.comment: the warrior emphasis: warriors, naturally, can improve THACO the most (printed p. 144).

bools.name: dewMonstersNoThacoLimit
bools.comment: the monster exception: monsters have no THACO limits (printed p. 144).

chains.name: dewPriestRow
chains.comment: the priest row band of Table 36: the defender's level minus the caster's level maps -7 or less to row 0, -4 to -6 to row 1, -1 to -3 to row 2, 0 to row 3, +1 to +3 to row 4, +4 to +6 to row 5, and +7 or more to row 6 (printed p. 143).

chains.name: dewRogueRow
chains.comment: the rogue row band of Table 36: -9 or less to row 0, -5 to -8 to row 1, -1 to -4 to row 2, 0 to row 3, +1 to +4 to row 4, and +5 or more to row 5 (printed p. 143).

chains.name: dewWarriorRow
chains.comment: the warrior row band of Table 36: -7 or less to row 0, -5 to -6 to row 1, -3 to -4 to row 2, -1 to -2 to row 3, 0 to row 4, +1 to +2 to row 5, +3 to +4 to row 6, +5 to +6 to row 7, +7 to +8 to row 8, and +9 or more to row 9 (printed p. 143).

chains.name: dewWizardRow
chains.comment: the wizard row band of Table 36: -6 or less to row 0, -1 to -5 to row 1, 0 to row 2, +1 to +5 to row 3, and +6 or more to row 4 (printed p. 143).

chains.name: dewT38Band
chains.comment: the Table 38 caster-level band (printed p. 144): levels 1-12 fall in band 0, 13-15 in band 1, 16-18 in band 2, 19-21 in band 3, 22-24 in band 4, 25-27 in band 5, 28-30 in band 6, and the band holds at 6 beyond 30; the penalty itself reads from the dewT38Penalty column by band.

tables.name: dewT36Grid
tables.comment: the Table 36 saving-throw grid (printed p. 143): the base save number by the defender's level minus the caster's level or Hit Dice (footnote 1), four groups in row bands - priest rows 0-6, rogue rows 7-12, warrior rows 13-22, wizard rows 23-27; the spell column excludes attacks that cause death, petrification or polymorph (the asterisk footnote).
col_comments: the paralyzation or death magic column: priest 10 down to 2, rogue 13 down to 8, warrior 16 down to 3, wizard 14 down to 8 across the defender-minus-caster bands (printed p. 143).
the petrification or polymorph column: priest 13 down to 5, rogue 12 down to 7, warrior 17 down to 4, wizard 13 down to 5 (printed p. 143).
the spell column (excluding death, petrification or polymorph attacks): priest 15 down to 7, rogue 15 down to 5, warrior 19 down to 6, wizard 12 down to 4 (printed p. 143).

tables.name: dewT38Grid
tables.comment: the Table 38 saving-throw penalty ladder (printed p. 144): the penalty by caster-level band - 0 for levels 1-12, minus 1 for 13-15, minus 2 for 16-18, minus 3 for 19-21, minus 4 for 22-24, minus 5 for 25-27, minus 6 for 28-30 and beyond.
col_comments: the penalty by band: 0, -1, -2, -3, -4, -5, -6 - a quicker and easier method than Table 36; if you use this table, do not use Table 36 (printed p. 144).

audit_comment: DMO Chapter 7 round one of five (printed pp. 142-144): the saving-throw doctrine - the group improvement limits (19, 21, 17, 21), the automatic failure on 3 or less with the deity ladders (2, 1, never), the adjusted-roll reading, the Wulf worked example (5 - 3 = 2); the Table 36 saves-by-caster-level grid with its four defender-minus-caster row-band chains; the Table 37 device casting levels; the Table 38 caster-level penalty ladder with its either-or rule; the Table 39 THACO limits with the automatic miss on 1.
